title: Constant-coefficient ring square for sequence-site evaluation
statement:
Let $C_n$ be arbitrary commutative rings with homomorphisms $\tau_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$. For every scheme $T$, put $B_{n,T}=\underline{C_n}_T$ on its small pro-etale site and $B_{\bullet,T}(n,H)=B_{n,T}(H)$ on the vertical sequence site. Use the actual constant-coefficient system operations of [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations] and the vertical restriction $e_{n,T}$ of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. For a scheme map $f:X\to Y$, let $F(H)=H\times_YX$, $F_\bullet=1_{\mathbf N}\times F$, and $\iota_{n,T}(H)=(n,H)$. Let $\Phi_f:B_{\bullet,Y}\to F_{\bullet,*}B_{\bullet,X}$ be the system structural ring map; let $\phi_{f,n}:B_{n,Y}\to F_*B_{n,X}$ be the right-adjoint transpose of the canonical constant-ring structure map $c^f_{C_n}:f^{-1}B_{n,Y}\to B_{n,X}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $a_T:B_{n,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}\iota_{n,T}^*B_{\bullet,T}$ be the specified evaluation identification. Under $F_\bullet\iota_{n,Y}=\iota_{n,X}F$, one has
$$\iota_{n,Y}^*(\Phi_f)\circ a_Y=F_*(a_X)\circ\phi_{f,n}.$$
In particular there is a unique natural isomorphism
$$d_{f,n}:e_{n,Y}f_{*,\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{*,n}e_{n,X}$$
whose hom and inverse are both the identity on each underlying section group $M_n(H\times_YX)$, with its specified $B_{n,Y}(H)$ action. These identities are natural in $M$, in $H$, and under every transition $C_m\to C_n$, after restriction of scalars. No finiteness or flatness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Put $\rho_{f,n}:B_{n,Y}\to F_*B_{n,X}$ for the constant-section map: it is the unique extension of $c\mapsto c$ from the constant presheaf. In the ring-sheaf adjunction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], write $\theta:\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}B_{n,Y},B_{n,X})\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(B_{n,Y},F_*B_{n,X})$. The structure map $c_{f,n}=c^f_{C_n}$ named in the item is defined there as $\varepsilon_f\circ f^{-1}(\rho_{f,n})$, i.e. $c_{f,n}=\theta^{-1}(\rho_{f,n})$ (the specified constant-section normalization); whether it is invertible plays no role. Consequently its right transpose is $\phi_{f,n}=\theta(c_{f,n})=\theta(\theta^{-1}(\rho_{f,n}))=\rho_{f,n}$. This is cancellation of an equivalence, and uses no finite-ring constant-map theorem.

source.place: Tag 09A5 (section-morphism), site inverse-image adjunction and its constant-section normalization; reference calculation in SemilinearProperOpenMatePasting.lean, constant_direct_image_map, lines 1685-1689.

proof.text: The evaluation of $B_{\bullet,T}$ at $(n,H)$ is literally $B_{n,T}(H)$, and the specified $a_T$ is the identity on that ring, by [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Also $F_\bullet\iota_{n,Y}(H)=(n,F(H))=\iota_{n,X}F(H)$, on arrows as well as objects. The defining structural map in [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations] has component $(\Phi_f)_{(n,H)}=(\rho_{f,n})_H$. Thus the left side of the required square has component $(\rho_{f,n})_H\circ\mathrm{id}$, and the right side has component $\mathrm{id}\circ(\phi_{f,n})_H$. Step 1 identifies these components. Equality at every object is equality of the natural transformations, proving the displayed ring square.

source.place: Tag 03D6 (definition-pushforward), restriction along the structural ring map; reference section calculation in SemilinearProperOpenMatePasting.lean, level_push_evaluation_normalized, lines 1765-1788.

proof.text: Fix $M$, $H$, $b\in B_{n,Y}(H)$ and $x\in M_n(F(H))$. The underlying abelian section group of each composite is $M_n(F(H))$. By the direct-image action formula of [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] and the system direct-image definition of [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations], its scalar action in the first composite is $(\Phi_f)_{(n,H)}(b)x$ after the identity evaluation identification. In the second it is $(\phi_{f,n})_H(b)x$. Step 2 makes these equal for every $b,x$. Therefore $x\mapsto x$ is additive and $B_{n,Y}(H)$-linear in both directions. These maps define module maps on sections without choosing any lift in $C_m$ of an element of $C_n$. In Lean reuse level_push_evaluation_normalized in the recorded operations module: its complete proof composes module pushforward-composition and coefficient-equality isomorphisms, giving these identity maps in both directions. Apply push_eq to the specified system direct image. No new existence statement is introduced.

source.place: Tag 03D6 (definition-pushforward), clause (1), sectionwise action by restriction of scalars.

proof.text: For $h:H'\to H$, each composite has the same underlying restriction $M_n(F(h)):M_n(F(H))\to M_n(F(H'))$; hence its naturality square for the identity maps reads $M_n(F(h))(x)=M_n(F(h))(x)$. For a system morphism $u:M\to N$, the corresponding square reads $u_n(F(H))(x)=u_n(F(H))(x)$. The sectionwise definition of module-sheaf morphisms in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] therefore turns the maps of Step 3 into natural transformations in $M$, mutually inverse because their composites are $x\mapsto x$. This constructs $d_{f,n}$ and its inverse. If $d'$ has the required normalization, its hom agrees with this hom on every $M,H,x$, so the underlying sheaf maps agree, hence the module maps and natural transformations agree. The inverse is forced by the inverse identities, proving uniqueness. The uniqueness clause is proved by Iso.ext, natural-transformation extensionality, and extensionality of the section linear maps, comparing the two identity normalizations.

source.place: Tag 03CW (definition-sheaf-modules), sectionwise morphisms, and Tag 03D6 (definition-pushforward); agent-written identity/naturality calculation.

proof.text: For m >= n, apply the naturality of the already constructed system coefficient map Phi_f to the horizontal arrow (n,H) -> (m,H). Its components are rho_{f,n} and rho_{f,m} by the specified normalization. The system ring restrictions are exactly the composite coefficient maps t_{m,n}. Thus naturality gives t_{m,n,Y} followed by rho_{f,n} equal to rho_{f,m} followed by F_*(t_{m,n,X}); Step 1 substitutes phi for rho. This reuses the existing constant-section/sheafification construction rather than repeating it. For the module transition, the definition of direct image sends a horizontal restriction to M applied to the image horizontal arrow. The base-change functor is the identity on the index and preserves the identity of H, so this is precisely the horizontal restriction of M at F(H). The normalization of the chosen comparison makes its hom and inverse the identity on sections; composing those identities with the restriction gives both asserted HEq equations. The calculation works uniformly for equality indices and composite transitions, without flatness, surjectivity or finiteness assumptions.
